headline: A seagrass planting machine built from a modified potato planter
standfirst: Hand-planting seagrass costs about £45 a square metre. This rig, welded together in a shed in Cornwall, does it for under six.

image.alt: A towed planting frame on the deck of a small workboat

body.text: The prototype looks exactly like what it is: a farm implement that has been dragged into the sea. It tows behind a small workboat, opens a shallow furrow in soft sediment, drops seed at a controlled rate and closes the furrow behind itself.
Everybody kept designing something new. The agricultural sector solved this in about 1890.
Germination rates in the first trial plot came in at 31 per cent, against roughly 40 per cent for hand-planting. At an eighth of the cost, that trade is easy to make.
